card: This pull request cleans up the functional test p2p_node_network_limited.py by correcting block height calculations in log messages and replacing an unnecessary ensure_for loop with direct assertions. Because blocks are not subject to trickle delays, a single ping/pong roundtrip reliably drains in-flight messages. The change addresses review feedback from PR #36446 to simplify test logic and contains no production code changes.
evidence: Commit fa13e8954d explains: 'NODE_NETWORK_LIMITED_MIN_BLOCKS includes two blocks of buffer, so the "tip-288" and "tip-289" comments were wrong. Also, the first mined block is at height 1, not height 2.'
Commit fadcd0b64e notes: 'There is no "trickle delay" for blocks, so a single ping should be sufficient to drain any possible in-flight blocks.'
problem: Log messages in the test miscalculated block heights relative to the chain tip, and an unnecessary ensure_for wait loop added confusion when checking that a node did not request blocks from a limited peer.

risk.why: A mistake could introduce test flakes or false failures in the p2p_node_network_limited functional test.

summary: Cleans up the functional test p2p_node_network_limited.py by correcting inaccurate block height references in test log messages and replacing an ensure_for polling loop with direct assertions. A single ping/pong cycle drains any in-flight block messages without needing polling for a duration.
